Solve for $x$ in the figure above given that $\angle AOC$ is complementary to $\angle COD.$
captured.worked_solution:
From the diagram, we have 

$$
m\angle AOC=x + 24^{\circ}
$$

and 

$$
m\angle COD=3x.
$$

  

Since $\angle AOC$ is complementary to $\angle COD,$ we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x+{24}^{∘})+3x & ={90}^{∘} \\ 4x+{24}^{∘} & ={90}^{∘} \\ 4x & ={66}^{∘} \\ x & ={16.5}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$
captured.knowledge_point: Finding an Unknown Quantity Using Complementary Angles

candidates.:question/problem:
Calculate $x$, given that $\angle{A}$ and $\angle{B}$ are complementary, and that
$m\angle{A} = 3x, \qquad m\angle{B} = 4x-8^\circ\,$.
candidates.:question/worked-solution:
Since angles $\angle{A}$ and $\angle{B}$ are complementary, we have

$$
m \angle A + m \angle B = 90^\circ
$$

Hence, we can solve for $x$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}
m∠A + m∠B &= 90^{∘} \\
3x + (4x - 8^{∘}) &= 90^{∘} \\
7x - 8^{∘} &= 90^{∘} \\
7x &= 98^{∘} \\
x &= 14^{∘}
\end{aligned}
$$
